claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, which the post describes as TypeSafe AI's SystemOne model, in the week before this post (dated 2026-09-25).
Jev is TypeSafe AI's SystemOne model.
TypeSafe's Jev provides a set of AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
Jev's decision-making primitives are confidence scoring, multiple choice (`choice()`), and yes/no (`noul()`) questions, plus rubric scoring (`score()`).

Jev's decision-making primitives are the perfect complement to agentic work, and combined with Pulumi the gap between designing ideal infrastructure and deploying it to production practically vanishes.
Agents can now handle infrastructure provisioning and day-to-day scaling and reliability decisions on users' behalf.
GeoDeploy pairs Jev's confidence-scored decisions with the Pulumi Automation API to place and scale Kubernetes across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
GeoDeploy (github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy) is released as open source.
The GitHub repository pulumi/devx-geodeploy exists and contains the GeoDeploy example.
The Pulumi Automation API docs exist at /docs/iac/automation-api/.
The link target /automation/ (Pulumi Automation API page) exists.
TypeSafe Jev docs exist at https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction.
Pulumi's X account handle is @PulumiCorp at https://x.com/PulumiCorp.
A free Pulumi account can be created at https://app.pulumi.com/signup.
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes and picks the best one for each geo.

In GeoDeploy's division of labor, the TypeScript app takes in the request, fetches live pricing, and does all the math without making judgment calls; Jev decides which region wins and which modules to use without doing arithmetic, generating code, or inventing region names; Pulumi provisions clusters, registries, workloads, and DNS without deciding anything.
GeoDeploy lists every region with managed Kubernetes and uses great-circle distance as its coverage measure.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog, normalized into a single quote format.
GeoDeploy's deterministic TypeScript bin-packs pods onto nodes, filters out instance types that don't match the image's architecture, and computes a monthly cost for each candidate region.

GeoDeploy composes a Pulumi program from a curated registry of typed modules covering EKS, AKS, or GKE; ECR, ACR, or Artifact Registry; ingress; DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare; and observability.
GeoDeploy uses the Pulumi Automation API to run a preview and then an update, with one stack per region.
GeoDeploy will not run provisioning unless the user's cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes a `plan.json` and `plan.md` containing the full decision record, and a web UI shows the deployment on a live globe.
Jev doesn't return free text; it returns typed answers with calibrated confidence through three primitives (`choice()`, `score()`, `noul()`).
Jev's `choice()` primitive picks one option from a closed list and returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence.
Jev's `score()` primitive rates something against a rubric the caller describes; GeoDeploy uses 10 levels.
Jev's `noul()` primitive answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
Jev only ever selects from closed sets in GeoDeploy and never writes code or does arithmetic, so a hallucinated region like `us-west-9` or a made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.
For each geo, GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates along with the constraints and the image's architecture.

In a single call per geo, GeoDeploy asks Jev for one region selection (`choice`), five quality scores (`score`: coverage, cost fit, maturity, sprawl risk, architecture consistency), two hard checks (`noul`: data residency satisfied and enough capacity), and a fallback region (`choice`).
GeoDeploy's `packages/decide/src/questions.ts` exports `buildStageAQuestions` and imports `choice`, `noul`, and `score` from `@typesafe-ai/sdk`.
The Jev `noul()` function takes a question string and an object with `true` and `false` keys describing the outcomes.

The `@typesafe-ai/sdk` package exposes a `TypeSafeClient` class whose `systemOne({ state, questions })` method returns a result with an `answers` object, where each answer exposes `.choice`, `.score`, `.noul`, and `.confidence` fields.
TypeSafe's advice on writing rubrics is to "describe situations, not degrees."

Each of the 10 GeoDeploy rubric levels is a concrete scenario, running from "Serves users on a different continent with no nearby presence" up to "In-geo with multiple availability zones, directly in or adjacent to the demand geo's primary population center."
The options passed to `choice()` are the priced candidates themselves, keyed by ID, so Jev cannot answer with a region that isn't on the list.
GeoDeploy's ranking runs on weight profiles: latency-optimized (the default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.
Because ranking weights live in code, GeoDeploy's ranking can be re-tuned without calling Jev again.

GeoDeploy's `WEIGHT_PROFILES` set weights (cost, coverage, maturity, sprawl, archConsistency) of latency-optimized 0.13/0.48/0.17/0.10/0.12, balanced 0.25/0.25/0.20/0.12/0.18, residency-first 0.12/0.12/0.38/0.23/0.15, and failure-domain 0.08/0.17/0.48/0.15/0.12, with sprawl subtracted in the composite formula.
Every extra cloud provider means more credentials, tooling, and on-call runbooks.
In GeoDeploy, cluster and registry modules follow directly from the provider (AWS always means EKS and ECR), and Jev decides only ingress posture, autoscaling posture, and node-pool sizing tier.

GeoDeploy's confidence gate thresholds are: data residency 0.95 (hard reject on failure); region for a new cluster 0.90 (top three candidates flagged for a human to choose); region when a stack already exists 0.75 (keep the existing region); ingress or autoscaling module 0.85 (use the registry default); node-pool sizing tier 0.60 (use the bin-packing result); region pick, residency, or capacity global floor 0.50 (drop the AI path for that geo).

GeoDeploy's `packages/decide/src/engine.ts` applies a residencyOk hard gate at 0.95 using `applyGate` and `GATE_THRESHOLDS.residencyOk`, and throws `AiPathAborted` on failure; it then validates that the selected region ID is one of the shortlisted candidates.
Each `AiPathAborted` in GeoDeploy carries the full attempt (state, questions, and answers), so even a rejected answer ends up in the audit trail.

If a gate check fails, the API times out or returns an error, or the upstream can't be reached, GeoDeploy switches to a deterministic fallback that compares prices across providers while still enforcing residency and constraint checks.
The `geodeploy explain` command shows why each region won.

When self-driving mode is enabled with `geodeploy monitor`, GeoDeploy periodically checks each deployment's CPU utilization and asks Jev one joint question across all regions with options `no-change`, `scale-up:<geo>`, `scale-down:<geo>`, or `shift:<from>-><to>`, plus a separate check on disruption risk.
In GeoDeploy's self-driving mode, code (not Jev) computes the actual node-count changes.

In GeoDeploy's self-driving mode, above 0.85 confidence the resize is applied automatically; between 0.70 and 0.85 it is suggested for a human to approve; below 0.70 GeoDeploy ignores Jev's pick and falls back to a deterministic per-region rule based on observed utilization.

CPU utilization alone makes a poor autoscaling metric; once a traffic baseline is established it is usually paired with other signals such as median end-to-end request latency, error rates, or application-specific metrics.
To get started with GeoDeploy, a user needs only access to Jev and a cloud provider.

The GeoDeploy web UI shows the us-east deployment on a live globe, and its decision panel for the us-east geo shows region selection plus coverage, cost, maturity, sprawl, and architecture scores with their confidence.
